# Hark

I set the rake aside,  
let it lie askew,  
for there’s nothing to rearrange,  
nothing else to pursue—  
with the scent of damp earth and composted leaves,  
and light’s scattered glints in dew droplets that weave,  
only I am superfluous here,  
whatever I might believe;  

not this, not that, the self I deny—  
nothing to grasp—nothing to tie.
